parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Nickel is a transition element. Sodium is an element in Group I of the Periodic Table. Nickel has a higher melting and boiling point than sodium. Give two other ways in which the physical properties of nickel differ from the physical properties of sodium. 1 ................................................................................................................................................. 2 ................................................................................................................................................. [2]

ms.label: 8(a)
ms.text:
one mark each for any two of:
•
nickel has high(er) density or reverse argument for sodium
•
nickel forms coloured compounds or reverse argument for sodium
•
nickel hard(er) or reverse argument for sodium

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) A steel spoon can be electroplated with nickel. The apparatus is shown.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Choose a word from the list which describes the nickel rod. Draw a circle around your answer. anion anode cathode cation electrolyte [1]

ms.label: 8(b)(ii)
ms.text:
pure nickel rod gets smaller (1)
spoon gets silvery / shiny / shinier(1)

ms.label: 8(b)(iii)
ms.text: makes object more attractive / makes object more resistant to corrosion / makes object (surface) harder

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) A compound of nickel has the formula NiC 4 O 4 . Complete the table to calculate the relative molecular mass of NiC 4 O 4 . atom number of atoms relative atomic mass nickel 1 59 1 × 59 = 59 carbon 12 oxygen 16 relative molecular mass = .............................. [2]

ms.label: 8(d)
ms.text:
171 (2)
If two marks not scored, allow 1 mark for C = 4 × 12 / 48 OR O = 4 ×16 / 64

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) The table shows the rates of reaction of four metals with steam. metal rate of reaction magnesium fast nickel slow sodium very fast tin very slow Put the four metals in order of their reactivity. Put the least reactive metal first. [2]

ms.label: 8(e)
ms.text:
tin < nickel < magnesium < sodium (2)
IF two marks not scored, 1 mark for one adjacent pair reversed.
